Where the Checks Come From

Source: vignettes/check-sources.qmd

Every checktor check rests on a source, and the source sets its severity. This page maps each check to its authority, links the exact section wherever one exists, and gives the severity that authority earns. For the full argument and the exemptions, read the check’s help page, such as ?lab_option_changes.

Read the severity

Severity tells you what kind of authority stands behind a check.

  • policy is a rule CRAN enforces. Breaking one can get a package rejected, and a policy finding counts against overall health. Most of these rules are written in the CRAN Repository Policy or Writing R Extensions, the two documents CRAN treats as binding. Some mirror a CRAN incoming check, one of the NOTEs that R CMD check --as-cran raises against a submission. For a few long-standing reviewer requirements that neither manual states, the CRAN Cookbook is the written record. Restoring options(), par() and the working directory is the clearest case. It is among the most common reasons a package is sent back, and neither manual mentions it.
  • robustness is a real defect that CRAN will still accept, such as a detectCores() that can return NA. It counts toward overall health too, because the defect is real whether or not CRAN objects to it.
  • opinion is a convention that experienced maintainers and reviewers tend to ask for, with nothing enforcing it. checktor reports it but leaves it out of overall health, which by default counts policy and robustness alone.

The Source column in each table below gives the authority. Many conventions are written down in the CRAN Cookbook, the R Contributor guide to the problems that get packages sent back. Where it has a recipe, the column links to it. For checks with no citable source, the column reads “No formal rule”, “No rule” or “Convention only”.

Which checks run

Most checks run every time. Some depend on the machine. When one of those cannot run, checktor() reports it as skipped rather than passed, so good overall health never rests on a check that did not happen. The skipped column of tidy() marks it, and metadata$skipped_checks lists it. Checks are also skipped when their input cannot be read. If R cannot read DESCRIPTION, every check that reads its fields is skipped, and description_file reports the problem as a policy finding. If Authors@R cannot be read, identifier_format is skipped.

Others run only when you call them. Nothing asked for them, so they are not skipped, and metadata$on_request_checks lists them so you can find them.

Check Runs Why
url_liveness at the console It fetches every URL, so it stays off in scripts and under R CMD check, where the network would decide the result. options(checktor.url_check = TRUE) runs it everywhere.
spelling with a backend It needs aspell or hunspell installed. options(checktor.spelling = FALSE) turns it off and reports it as skipped. options(checktor.disable = "spelling") or Config/checktor/disable: spelling leaves it out of the run entirely.
cran_comments_file when you call it cran-comments.md belongs to the submission workflow rather than to the package.
title_starts_with_article when you call it No authority supports it, so it stays available without joining the run.
description_function_quotes when you call it No authority supports it either, and Writing R Extensions points the other way.
cph_role when you call it ?person says authors who are natural persons hold copyright by default, so most packages need no cph role.
format_names when you call it CRAN accepts JSON, HTML, SQL and the other format names written bare, so quoting them is a matter of style.

Every other check runs always, and new checks join the run unless their row in the registry says otherwise. No check goes missing because someone forgot to switch it on.

Code checks

Check Severity Source
seed_setting policy CRAN Policy: a package “should not modify the global environment”, and set.seed() writes .Random.seed there. Recipe: Setting a Specific Seed.
print_cat_usage policy Cookbook: Using print()/cat(): diagnostic output belongs in message() or warning(), which a user can suppress. Reviewers require it, though neither manual states it.
option_changes policy Cookbook: Change of Options, Graphical Parameters and Working Directory: restore anything a function changes, with on.exit(). Neither manual states this, but it is among the most common reasons a package is sent back.
warn_option policy Cookbook: Setting options(warn = -1): the same requirement, for the warning level.
home_writing policy CRAN Policy: “Packages should not write in the user’s home filespace … nor anywhere else on the file system apart from the R session’s temporary directory”. Recipe: Writing Files and Directories to the Home Filespace.
globalenv_mod policy CRAN Policy: “Packages should not modify the global environment (user’s workspace).” Recipe: Writing to the .GlobalEnv.
installed_packages policy CRAN Policy: a package must not install other packages when it runs. Recipe: Calling installed.packages().
software_install policy CRAN Policy: a package must not download and install external software at load or run time. Recipe: Installing Software.
core_usage policy CRAN Policy: “If running a package uses multiple threads/cores it must never use more than two simultaneously”. Recipe: Using more than 2 Cores.
sys_setenv policy No clause mentions environment variables, but they are session state in the same way options() are, so the same restore-on-exit requirement applies. See Cookbook: Change of Options, Graphical Parameters and Working Directory.
tf_usage robustness No binding rule, but a documented one in Cookbook: T/F Instead of TRUE/FALSE. T and F are ordinary variables (see ?logical) that code can rebind, so they make unsafe stand-ins.
library_in_pkg robustness WRE: Package Dependencies: package code should reach dependencies through Imports and ::, not attach them with library().
detect_cores_robustness robustness No formal rule. ?detectCores states it returns “NA if the answer is unknown”, and the arithmetic that usually follows then crashes.
hardcoded_credentials robustness No formal rule. Tokens and keys committed to a package are public the moment it reaches CRAN, and must be revoked.
internal_ns robustness CRAN asks you to omit one colon, since ::: reaches an object whose author may change it. R CMD check reports it too, under dependencies in R code.
temp_cleanup opinion Cookbook: Leaving Files in the Temporary Directory. R removes tempdir() when the session ends, so a temporary file nobody unlink()ed breaks no rule. That keeps this check advisory.

DESCRIPTION checks

Check Severity Source
description_file policy WRE: The DESCRIPTION file: “Fields start with an ASCII name immediately followed by a colon” and “Continuation lines … start with a space or tab”. R CMD build and R CMD INSTALL stop on a file that breaks this, or that a blank line splits in two.
description_fields policy CRAN incoming check: it NOTEs “Unknown, possibly misspelled, fields in DESCRIPTION”, allowing Config/ and a few other prefixes. Remotes is the usual one. CRAN Policy wants strong dependencies “available from CRAN or the Bioconductor software repository”.
description_placeholders policy CRAN incoming check: it NOTEs “DESCRIPTION fields with placeholder content”, the Title, Description, Author or Maintainer a usethis or package.skeleton() template wrote.
software_names policy WRE: The DESCRIPTION file: “Refer to other packages and external software in single quotes”. Recipe: Formatting Software Names.
language_names policy WRE: The DESCRIPTION file: the same rule, for programming languages and statistical software such as Python, Java, MATLAB and SAS. Recipe: Formatting Software Names.
description_quoted_quotes policy WRE: The DESCRIPTION file: double quotes are for book titles and similar, and software names take single quotes. The format names format_names covers are left out, since CRAN accepts them bare. Recipe: Formatting Software Names.
license policy CRAN Policy: an invalid or unrecognized License field is a rejection. Recipe: LICENSE files.
license_file_unneeded policy Cookbook: LICENSE files: CRAN does “not need” + file LICENSE “and the file as these are part of R”, unless the file adds attribution requirements or restrictions. R CMD check NOTEs the pointer on a license that takes no extension, and the incoming check NOTEs it on one that does, such as GPL-3.
authors policy CRAN Policy: a placeholder or malformed Authors@R, including a missing maintainer, is a rejection. Recipe: Using Authors@R.
title_case policy WRE: The DESCRIPTION file: the Title “should use title case”. The --as-cran incoming check flags one that does not. Recipe: Title Case.
title_package_name policy WRE: The DESCRIPTION file: “Do not repeat the package name: it is often used prefixed by the name.” The incoming check NOTEs a Title that is the name or starts with it. Only the name alone and name: are flagged, since CRAN routinely accepts a name that is an ordinary word, as in “Survival Analysis”.
date_format policy WRE: The DESCRIPTION file: “the ‘yyyy-mm-dd’ format of the ISO 8601 standard is strongly recommended”. The incoming check also flags a stale or future date.
version_format policy WRE: The DESCRIPTION file: a Version is “a sequence of at least two … non-negative integers”. The incoming check flags a leading zero or an implausible value.
encoding_utf8 policy WRE: The DESCRIPTION file: a non-ASCII DESCRIPTION “should contain an ‘Encoding’ field”. The incoming check NOTEs any value other than UTF-8 as deprecated, latin1 and latin2 included.
description_starts_with policy WRE: The DESCRIPTION file: “It is good practice not to start with the package name, ‘This package’ or similar”. The incoming check flags it.
references policy CRAN incoming check: it NOTEs a URL outside <...>, a DOI not written <doi:prefix/suffix> or given as a publisher link, and an arXiv id where the submission checklist asks for the arXiv DOI <doi:10.48550/arXiv.ID>. Recipe: References.
identifier_format policy CRAN incoming check: it NOTEs a malformed ORCID or ROR identifier in Authors@R.
license_year robustness No binding rule. Leaving <YEAR> or <COPYRIGHT HOLDER> in the LICENSE template puts a placeholder where the copyright notice belongs. Recipe: LICENSE files.
spelling opinion CRAN incoming check (aspell), but it needs a spell-check backend and is noisy, so checktor keeps it advisory.
acronyms opinion Cookbook: Explaining Acronyms. Reviewers ask for an acronym to be spelled out once, but nothing enforces it.
cph_role opinion ?person: cph is for copyright holders, and authors who are natural persons hold copyright by default without it. CRAN Policy asks only that ownership be clear, which a Copyright field also achieves. Runs on request.
format_names opinion No rule. WRE: The DESCRIPTION file asks for quotes around software, and JSON, HTML, XML, CSS, YAML, TOML, Markdown, LaTeX, TeX and SQL are formats. C++, Fortran and Tcl are written either way. In a census of CRAN in September 2026, packages accepted at new-package review in the previous 18 months wrote these bare 62% of the time, against 28% for the names language_names checks. Runs on request.
description_length opinion Cookbook: Description Length. Reviewers find a one-line Description thin and ask for more.
title_length opinion WRE: The DESCRIPTION file: “Some package listings may truncate the title to 65 characters”. That is a display width rather than a limit, so a Title that fills it exactly still shows in full, and nothing rejects a longer one.
title_redundant_phrases opinion Convention only. Phrases like “R package to” are redundant in a Title.
title_starts_with_article opinion No rule. The real CRAN rule, which description_starts_with enforces, concerns the opening of the Description. Kept callable but off by default.
description_function_quotes opinion No rule, and Writing R Extensions points the other way. Kept callable but off by default.

Documentation checks

Check Severity Source
suggested_in_examples policy WRE: Suggested packages: a package from Suggests used in an example must be guarded so the example still runs without it.
rd_bibliography policy WRE: Bibliographic citations and references: R 4.6’s \bibcitet{}, \bibcitep{} and \bibshow{} read the package bibliography. R CMD check warns “Could not find bibentries for the following keys” and notes “Bibentries cited but not shown”, and --as-cran notes a REFERENCES file at the top level as non-standard.
roxygen_usage robustness No binding rule. Functions tagged @export that never reached NAMESPACE are not exported. Recipe: Repeated Rejections of Issues in Manuals If Using roxygen2.
unexported_example_ns robustness No formal rule. Examples that reach for an unexported object error when they run.
rd_bibliography_files robustness WRE: Bibliographic citations and references keeps the bibliography as inst/REFERENCES.R or inst/REFERENCES.bib, which “needs bibtex to be installed”. Nothing checks either. Without bibtex in Suggests, a .bib fails a build that installs only what is declared, and one outside inst/ is never installed for another package’s pkg::key.
value_tags opinion WRE: Documenting functions describes \value{}, and Cookbook: Missing -tags in .Rd-files is the recipe reviewers cite, but R CMD check does not require it.
example_structure opinion Cookbook: Structuring of Examples. \dontrun{} should wrap only code that cannot run inside a check.
donttest_vs_dontrun opinion Cookbook: Structuring of Examples: \donttest{} is the wrapper for examples that merely run long, where many reach for \dontrun{} instead.
missing_examples opinion Cookbook: Structuring of Examples. Exported functions are expected to carry an \examples{} block.
commented_examples opinion Convention only. Commenting out a whole \examples{} block leaves it demonstrating nothing.

Example, vignette and demo checks

These checks cover the code outside R/ that CRAN reads, where several of the most common rejections land. Maintainers have received each rule below, verbatim, in a reply from CRAN.

Check Severity Source
example_interactive policy Cookbook: Structuring of Examples: a function that only runs interactively belongs in if (interactive()), so a reader sees it is not for a script, rather than in \dontrun{}. In \donttest{} it does more harm, because R CMD check --as-cran runs that code, where a prompt errors and an app waits for input.
example_installs policy Cookbook: Installing Software: do not install packages from a function, an example or a vignette.
example_writes policy Cookbook: Writing Files and Directories to the Home Filespace: an example, vignette or test may write only to tempdir().
example_state policy Cookbook: Change of Options, Graphical Parameters and Working Directory: restore options(), par() and the working directory changed in an example, vignette or demo.
example_internal_ns policy CRAN asks you to omit one colon, since ::: reaches an object whose behavior the author may change.
example_tf_usage robustness Cookbook: T/F Instead of TRUE/FALSE: T and F “should not be used as variable names in your code, examples, tests or vignettes”. The same rule as tf_usage, applied to examples, vignettes and demos.
example_unparseable robustness Reviewers send this rejection verbatim: “Unexecutable code in man/…Rd”. WRE: Documenting functions lets \dontrun{} text be something other than R, but reviewers run examples with it included, and R CMD check never parses it, so a missing bracket or a <your key> placeholder there goes unseen.

General checks

Check Severity Source
code_exercised policy CRAN incoming check: --as-cran WARNs “No examples, no tests, no vignettes” for a package that exports code and includes none of the three. CRAN Policy asks that “the checks that are left do exercise all the features of the package”.
citation_file policy CRAN incoming check: --as-cran NOTEs an inst/CITATION that calls the old-style citEntry() or personList(), and lists calls to packageDescription(), library() and require(). WRE: CITATION files: “It is desirable (and essential for CRAN) that the CITATION file does not contain calls to functions such as packageDescription which assume the package is installed”.
package_size policy CRAN Policy: CRAN limits the size of the built tarball. Recipe: Package Size, which gives the practical figures.
url_liveness robustness CRAN incoming check: --as-cran fetches URLs and NOTEs 404s and redirects. It runs at the console and stays off in scripts and checks, where the network would decide the result.
readme_links robustness No formal rule. Relative README links whose targets are excluded from the tarball break on the package page.
urls opinion Convention only. Preferring https:// is good advice, but CRAN’s NOTE is about broken URLs rather than the scheme.
news_file opinion Convention only. NEWS files are expected but not required.
cran_comments_file opinion Convention only. cran-comments.md belongs to the submission workflow rather than to the package, so this check runs only when you call it.

CRAN policy checks

Check Severity Source
browser_calls policy CRAN Policy: checks run non-interactively, so a debugging leftover such as browser() must not remain.
file_operations policy CRAN Policy: “Packages should not write … anywhere … apart from the R session’s temporary directory”. Recipe: Writing Files and Directories to the Home Filespace.
network_operations policy CRAN Policy: “Packages which use Internet resources should fail gracefully with an informative message if the resource is not available”.
system_calls robustness No flat rule. Raw system() and system2() calls need review for portability, so they are not automatic violations.

Leave two recipes to people

checktor has a check for every CRAN Cookbook recipe that describes a pattern in your sources. The two recipes without one describe things that no reading of the sources can settle.

Overall Checktime concerns a measurement. The NOTE reads “Overall checktime 20 min > 10 min”, and nothing in your sources tells how long they will take to run. R CMD check reports the figure, and the fix is fewer or smaller examples, vignettes and tests.

Communicating with CRAN is advice on writing to CRAN, including copying cran-submissions@r-project.org and explaining yourself in cran-comments.md. Its one checkable part, whether that file exists, is cran_comments_file.

Resolve a disagreement

Severity records where a check’s authority sits, not how strongly checktor feels about it. Several checks are opinion because no authority backs them in either direction. Of those, title_starts_with_article, description_function_quotes and format_names stay callable but are left out of the default run for that reason. cph_role stays out because its own source says most authors need no cph role. cran_comments_file stays out because it asks about a submission workflow rather than the package.

If a finding contradicts your reading of the policy, look at its severity first. Opinion findings open a conversation and require nothing. To turn a check off for one package, list it in Config/checktor/disable in that package’s DESCRIPTION. To turn it off for every package, set options(checktor.disable = ...), for example in .Rprofile. Either way, the check does not run at all.
